Calcium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ca and atomic number 20.
In what year was Sam Altman born?
Sam Altman: Altman attended Stanford University for two years before he dropped out and co-founded Loopt, a smartphone geosocial networking service.
In what year was Bayes' theorem discovered?
Bayes' theorem: The theorem was developed in the 18th century by Bayes and independently by Pierre-Simon Laplace.
Genetics: Gregor Mendel. Genetics is the study of genes, genetic variation, and heredity in organisms.
Doxycycline: Pfizer. It is used to treat bacterial pneumonia, acne, chlamydia infections, Lyme disease, cholera, typhus, and syphilis, and is sometimes used to prevent malaria.
Which country is Bombardier Challenger 600 series from?
Bombardier Challenger 600 series: Canada. At the end of 1975, Canadair began funding the development of LearStar 600, and then bought the design for a wide-cabin business jet in April 1976.
Who is credited with discovering Hassium?
GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research
Hassium: GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research. Hassium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Hs and atomic number 108.
Who is credited with discovering HD 209458 b?
HD 209458 b: Michel Mayor. It is sometimes informally called Osiris.
Who is credited with discovering Osmium?
Osmium: Smithson Tennant. Osmium (from Ancient Greek ὀσμή (osmḗ) 'smell') is a chemical element; it has symbol Os and atomic number 76.
One of the very few semiaquatic vipers in the world, which venomous pit viper native to the southeastern United States is often found coiled near slow-moving lakes, streams, and marshes?
Agkistrodon piscivorus is a species of venomous snake, a pit viper in the subfamily Crotalinae of the family Viperidae.

With more than 140 species spread across 16 genera in oceans worldwide, these small forage fish are usually classified as oily fish, and a few South American species live only in fresh water — name this fish?
Anchovy are small, common forage fish of the family Engraulidae.
Excavated in Argentina starting in 1989 under paleontologist José Bonaparte, this Late Cretaceous titanosaur weighed as much as 80 tons — which genus of giant sauropod?
Argentinosaurus (meaning "lizard from Argentina") is a genus of giant sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period in what is now Argentina.

Developed in Great Britain around the 1830s from breeds like the Talbot Hound, this scent hound — smaller than the similar-looking foxhound — was originally bred to hunt rabbits and hares — name the breed?
Beagle is a British breed of scent hound, similar in appearance to the much larger foxhound.
This insect order contains both cockroaches and termites — the latter now classified as a specialized, social lineage within the former group — what order is it?
Blattodea is an order of insects that contains cockroaches and termites.

More muscular and aggressive than the females of the species, this uncastrated adult male of Bos taurus has long symbolized power in religious sacrifice and features prominently in ranching and blood sports — which term describes him?
Bull is an intact (i.e., not castrated) adult male of the species Bos taurus (cattle).
This Mexican business magnate was ranked the richest person in the world by Forbes from 2010 to 2013, building his fortune through a sprawling conglomerate called Grupo Carso. Who is he?
Carlos Slim (born 28 January 1940) is a Mexican business oligarch, investor and philanthropist.
The principal sterol of all animals, it concentrates in the brain and spinal cord and is essential to every cell membrane — yet too much in the blood spells trouble. What is it?
Cholesterol is the principal sterol of all animals, distributed in body tissues, especially the brain and spinal cord, and in animal fats and oils.
This legless, non-venomous lizard native to Europe is often mistaken for a snake despite having smooth, non-overlapping scales and semi-fossorial burrowing habits — what is it called?
Common slow worm (Anguis fragilis) is a non-venomous species of legless lizard native to Europe.
Grown from tubers and known by the folk name 'sowbread,' this Primulaceae genus features flowers with distinctively upswept petals — which plant genus?
Cyclamen is a genus of 25 species of perennial flowering plants in the family Primulaceae.

Bred in the early twentieth century in Córdoba, Argentina, for hunting big game like wild boar and pumas, this large mastiff-type dog breed traces its ancestry partly to a now-extinct fighting dog — name the breed?
Dogo Argentino (plural Dogos Argentinos) is an Argentine breed of large dog of mastiff type.
Born to a mathematician father in Erlangen, this pioneering algebraist proved theorems connecting symmetry to conservation laws in physics — who is she?
Emmy Noether (23 March 1882 - 14 April 1935) was a German mathematician who made many important contributions to abstract algebra.
Despite its name, this highly sociable oceanic dolphin earned its label from a skull resembling the orca's — it can reach 20 feet and even forms mixed pods with bottlenose dolphins. What is it?
False killer whale (Pseudorca crassidens) is a species of oceanic dolphin that is the only extant representative of the genus Pseudorca.

This American mechanical engineer and pioneering management consultant wrote a 1909 book that Academy of Management fellows later voted the most influential management book of the entire 20th century — who was he?
Frederick Winslow Taylor (March 20, 1856 - March 21, 1915) was an American mechanical engineer.
This ancient metabolic pathway breaks glucose down into pyruvate through ten enzyme-catalyzed reactions in a cell's cytosol, generating ATP along the way. What process is it?
Glycolysis is the metabolic pathway that converts glucose (C6H12O6) into pyruvate and, in most organisms, occurs in the liquid part of cells (the cytosol).
About the size of a closed fist and tucked between the lungs, this four-chambered muscular organ pumps blood throughout the body — name it?
Heart is a muscular organ found in humans and other animals.
A colourless, ammonia-scented liquid with formula N2H4, this hazardous compound foams polymers, inflates airbags, and serves as a storable spacecraft propellant. What is it?
Hydrazine is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula N2H4.
Serving as the continuous analog of a summation, this fundamental calculus operation is used to compute areas, volumes, and displacement from velocity — name the mathematical concept?
Integral is the continuous analog of a sum, and is used to calculate areas, volumes, and their generalizations.
The youngest division chief in GM history, this engineer shepherded the Pontiac GTO before founding the company behind a famously gull-winged car — who was he?
John DeLorean (d-; January 6, 1925 - March 19, 2005) was an American engineer, inventor, and executive in the U.S.
Named after a 19th-century Russian neuropsychiatrist, which memory disorder features confabulation and amnesia from vitamin B1 deficiency, often following an episode of Wernicke encephalopathy?
Korsakoff syndrome (KS) is a disorder of the central nervous system characterized by amnesia, deficits in explicit memory, and confabulation.
One of only five people to win multiple Nobel Prizes, this American chemist and peace activist is the sole person to have received two unshared Nobels — one in Chemistry, one for Peace. Who is he?
Linus Pauling (February 28, 1901 - August 19, 1994) was an American chemist and peace activist.

This colorless, highly water-soluble inorganic salt forms hydrates holding up to 12 water molecules per unit, and its anhydrous form is industry's main source for producing a lightweight, silvery-white structural metal — which compound is it?
Magnesium chloride is an inorganic compound with the formula MgCl2.
First made in 1955 by bombarding einsteinium with alpha particles, this synthetic element 101 is named for the father of the periodic table — what is it?
Mendelevium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Md (formerly Mv) and atomic number 101.

Caused by a poxvirus spread through direct contact, this viral skin infection produces small raised pink lesions with a distinctive dimple in the center, usually clearing on its own within a year — name the condition?
Molluscum contagiosum (MC), sometimes called water warts, is a viral infection of the skin that results in small raised pink lesions with a dimple in the center.

Nicknamed for its terrifying rate of tissue destruction, this fast-spreading bacterial infection doesn't actually consume flesh — the bacteria instead release toxins that destroy it — what is this disease called?
Necrotizing fasciitis (NF), also known as flesh-eating disease or flesh-eating bacteria, is an infection that kills the body's soft tissue.

Encompassing 24 genera from baboons to colobus to langurs, this is the largest primate family, having diverged from a separate primate lineage 45 to 55 million years ago before apes split off from it too — which family?
Old World monkey are primates in the family Cercopithecidae.
Making up the order Psittaciformes, these birds are known for a strong curved beak, upright stance, and clawed feet, with a third of all species threatened by extinction — name the group?
Parrot (order Psittaciformes), also known as psittacines from the name of the type genus Psittacus, are birds with a strong curved beak, upright stance, and clawed feet.
One of nine essential amino acids we must eat rather than make ourselves, it's found in mammals' milk and acts as a direct precursor to the neuromodulator phenethylamine — which molecule is it?
Phenylalanine (symbol Phe or F) is an -amino acid with the formula C9H11NO2.

This natural process transfers pollen from a flower's anther to its stigma, enabling fertilization and seed production, carried out by everything from bees and bats to wind and water — what process is it?
Pollination is the transfer of pollen from an anther of a plant to the stigma of a plant, later enabling fertilisation and the production of seeds.

This psychiatric state describes an inability to distinguish reality from delusion, marked by symptoms like hallucinations and disorganized thinking, and can stem from conditions like schizophrenia or bipolar disorder — name the state?
Psychosis is the inability to distinguish what is or is not real.
This inflammatory disease typically develops two to four weeks after a streptococcal throat infection and can damage the heart valves in about half of cases — what is it?
Rheumatic fever (RF) is an inflammatory disease that can involve the heart, joints, skin, and brain.
After dropping out of Stanford and co-founding a startup later sold for over $40 million, this entrepreneur led Y Combinator before taking the helm of a leading AI company — who is he?
Sam Altman (born April 22, 1985) is an American entrepreneur and investor who has been the chief executive officer (CEO) of the artificial intelligence company OpenAI since 2019.
The smallest of Japan's six native dog breeds, this small, alert hunting dog's name literally translates to 'brushwood dog,' reflecting its original job of flushing game — which breed?
Shiba Inu (Japanese) is a breed of hunting dog from Japan.

Meaning 'pore bearer' in Greek, this phylum of sessile, filter-feeding marine invertebrates has tube-like bodies of jelly-like material sandwiched between thin cell layers, letting water circulate through countless pores — name the animal group?
Sponge are primarily marine invertebrates of the animal phylum Porifera (meaning 'pore bearer').

This amniote lineage — one of just two major branches alongside the reptile-and-bird clade — is marked by a single temporal opening behind the eye and gave rise to every mammal alive today — name the group?
Synapsida is a diverse group of tetrapod vertebrates that includes all mammals and their extinct relatives.
This genus of coniferous evergreen in the cypress family includes five species — two native to North America, three to eastern Asia — and is sister to the genus Thujopsis. Name the genus?
Thuja is a genus of coniferous tree or shrub in the Cupressaceae (cypress family).
The two major groups of these reptiles, side-necked and hidden-necked, differ in how they pull in the head — and they breathe air despite many living in water. What animal?
Turtle (order Testudines) are reptiles characterized by a special shell developed mainly from their ribs, as well as keratinized toothless beak.

This trailing vine of the gourd family bears a fruit that's botanically a 'pepo' — a hard-rinded berry with no internal divisions — and comes in more than 1,000 varieties, even seedless ones. What is it?
Watermelon (Citrullus lanatus) is a species of flowering plant in the family Cucurbitaceae, that has a large, edible fruit.
Adding or subtracting this number leaves any other number unchanged. In mathematical terms it is the additive what, of the integers and the reals?

0 is a number representing an empty quantity. Adding or subtracting 0 to any number leaves that number unchanged; in mathematical terminology 0 is the additive identity of the integers, rational numbers, real numbers and complex numbers.
Considered sacred by Hindus and Buddhists, this tree native to the Indian subcontinent is also known as bael and is the sole member of its genus — which species?
Aegle marmelos: Species of tree, considered sacred by Hindus. It is present in India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, and Nepal as a naturalized species.
With the general formula CnH2n+2 and every carbon-carbon bond single, methane is the simplest example of this class of hydrocarbons — what's it called?
Alkane: Type of saturated hydrocarbon compound.
This group of diseases occurs when misfolded proteins accumulate in body tissue, causing fatigue, swelling, and shortness of breath among roughly 36 distinct protein-driven types — what is it?
Amyloidosis: Metabolic disease involving abnormal deposited amyloid proteins.
Usually symptomless until it ruptures — causing sudden, severe abdominal or lower-back pain — this dangerous enlargement of the body's main artery is most common in the abdomen — what condition?
Aortic aneurysm: Excessive enlargement of the human aorta.
Born from acetylsalicylic acid, this everyday drug cools fevers within about 30 minutes and is taken long-term to fend off heart attacks and strokes by quieting platelets — what is it?

The most widespread bird in its family, found on every continent except Antarctica (where only stray vagrants appear), this species has blue upperparts, a deeply forked tail, and usually nests in man-made structures — what is it?
Barn swallow: Species of bird. The barn swallow (Hirundo rustica) is the most widespread species of swallow in the world, occurring on all continents, with vagrants reported even in Antarctica.
This interdisciplinary field examines moral questions raised by advances in biology, medicine, and biotechnology, touching everything from patient care to environmental policy — what is it called?
Bioethics: Study of the ethical issues emerging from advances in biology and medicine.
A synthetic group-7 transition metal made only in particle accelerators, this radioactive element honors a Danish physicist and sits at atomic number 107 — what is it?
Bohrium: Chemical element with atomic number 107 (Bh)

Known also as the Zambezi or Lake Nicaragua species, this aggressive fish can thrive in both salt and fresh water, having been tracked more than 1,100 kilometers up the Mississippi River — what animal is it?
Bull shark: Species of fish. Bull sharks are listed as vulnerable on the IUCN Red List.
Indigenous to the Hindu Kush mountains and grown across Asia and Africa largely for hashish production, this plant species carries far more THC than industrial hemp — which species is it?
Cannabis indica: Species of plant. Cannabis indica is an annual plant species in the family Cannabaceae indigenous to the Hindu Kush mountains of Southern Asia.
Its edible 'curd' is actually a dense head of undeveloped flower buds, and one variety grows its curds in spiral fractal patterns — which vegetable?
Cauliflower: Vegetable in the species Brassica oleracea.
Traceable to fairy tales that weren't classified this way until the seventeenth century, this genre spans picture books for toddlers to young-adult fiction for teens — what category of writing?
Children's literature: Stories, books, magazines, and poems primarily written for children.
This spore-forming, rod-shaped bacterium produces the most potent toxin known to science, causing a severe paralytic illness often linked to bulging canned food — what's its name?
Clostridium botulinum: Species of endospore forming bacterium.

This grayish-brown, wart-skinned amphibian (scientific name Bufo bufo) is found across most of Europe, hides by day, and hunts invertebrates at dusk, moving with a slow, ungainly walk or short jumps — which species?
Common toad: Species of amphibian. It belongs to a group of closely related species descended from a common ancestral line of toads and forming a species complex.
Originating in French cuisine and beloved in Spain, this breaded, deep-fried roll often reuses leftover roasted chicken or broth meat as its filling — what is it called?

Nicknamed the 'Wooden Wonder' for its mostly-timber airframe, this WWII British warplane was among the fastest operational aircraft of 1941 and later moonlighted as a high-speed courier for a national airline — what was it?
De Havilland Mosquito: British multi-role combat aircraft of WW2.
This category of mental health conditions involves an unconscious defense mechanism that fragments consciousness, memory, and identity to protect against traumatic stress — what is it called?
Dissociative disorder: Set of mental health conditions.
A pregnancy complication where the embryo attaches outside the uterus, classically presenting with abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding. What is this condition?
Ectopic pregnancy: Female reproductive system health issue.
A sympathomimetic stimulant often used to keep blood pressure up during anesthesia, this drug has also been tried for asthma, narcolepsy, and obesity — what is it?

Ranging from Northern Europe through Siberia to the Himalayas, this medium-sized wild cat is one of only four living species in its genus and can be found at elevations up to 5,500 meters — what animal is this?
Eurasian lynx: Species of medium-sized cat native to Eurasia.

Named for the physicist who reportedly asked 'but where is everybody?' at Los Alamos in 1950, this puzzle questions why we've found no evidence of alien civilizations despite the odds favoring them — what's it called?
Fermi paradox: Discrepancy of the lack of evidence for alien life despite its apparent likelihood.
Alongside James Watson, this English scientist co-authored the 1953 Nature paper unveiling DNA's double helix and later coined the phrase 'central dogma' — who is he?
Francis Crick: English physicist and biologist (1916–2004)

Published by Einstein in 1916 as a refinement of Newton's law of gravitation, this geometric framework describes gravity as curved spacetime, summed up by Wheeler as 'space-time tells matter how to move; matter tells space-time how to curve'?
General relativity: Theory of gravitation as curved spacetime. The relation is specified by the Einstein field equations, a system of second-order partial differential equations.
Despite its common name, this Eurasian wolf-like canid is more closely related to wolves and coyotes than to its African namesakes — what animal is it?
Published in 1931 by an Austrian logician, these two results proved that any consistent axiom system for arithmetic will always contain true statements it cannot prove — what are they called?
Gödel's incompleteness theorems: Limitative results in mathematical logic.
Dubbed 'the Gauss of modern mathematics,' this French polymath's work on the three-body problem uncovered the first chaotic deterministic system, laying the groundwork for chaos theory — who is he?
Henri Poincaré: French mathematician, physicist and engineer (1854–1912)
With red compound eyes set wider apart in females, this insect lays batches of about 100 eggs on decaying matter that hatch into maggots — which species?
Housefly: Species of insect. The housefly (Musca domestica) is a fly of the suborder Cyclorrhapha.
Distinguished by the male's large, transversely ridged curved horns, which wild goat species roams Eurasia and Africa?
This order of crustaceans includes both seafaring gribbles and the woodlice in your garden, with females brooding their young in a belly pouch called a marsupium. What is it?
Isopoda: Order of arthropods. The order is divided into eleven suborders.

This American physicist worked with Niels Bohr on nuclear fission and had a gift for coinages — "quantum foam," "wormhole," and the term that popularized "gravitationally collapsed objects." Who was he?
John Archibald Wheeler: American theoretical physicist (1911–2008)
Nicknamed 'The Professor' on The Chase, this record-breaking contestant won 74 consecutive games on a legendary quiz show in 2004 before eventually becoming its host — who is he?
Ken Jennings: American game show host (born 1974)
Known by common names like true lavender and English lavender despite not being native to England, this Mediterranean-basin plant belongs to the mint family — which species?
Lavandula angustifolia: Species of plant. Lavandula angustifolia, formerly L. officinalis, is a flowering plant in the family Lamiaceae, native to the Mediterranean basin.
A sweet, aromatic flavouring used in confectionery, tobacco, and pharmaceuticals comes from the root of which legume — though more than a couple of milligrams per kilo a day can cause trouble?
Painlessly swollen lymph nodes, drenching night sweats, and unexplained weight loss point to this family of white-blood-cell cancers, split mainly into Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin types — what is it?
Lymphoma: Hematologic cancer that affects lymphocytes.

The first woman to write a mathematics handbook and the first appointed as a university math professor, this Milanese scholar later traded calculus for four decades of theology and charity — who is she?
Maria Gaetana Agnesi: Italian mathematician and philanthropist (1718–1799)
Typically running 21 to 35 days, this coordinated dance of estrogen and progesterone prepares the uterine lining and releases an egg to make pregnancy possible — what is it?
Menstrual cycle: Natural changes in the human female reproductive system.
This twin-engine Soviet fighter, known to NATO as 'Fulcrum,' was built in the 1970s to counter American jets like the F-15 and F-16 — which aircraft is it?
Mikoyan MiG-29: Soviet twin-engine jet fighter aircraft. The Mikoyan MiG-29 (Russian: Микоян МиГ-29; NATO reporting name: Fulcrum) is a twin-engine fighter aircraft designed in the Soviet Union.

First identified from skulls found in a Dutch chalk quarry near Maastricht and initially mistaken for crocodile or whale bones, this giant marine lizard genus lived until 66 million years ago — which genus is it?
Mosasaurus: Extinct genus of marine lizard from the Late Cretaceous.
Colloquially known as a moon, this type of astronomical body orbits a planet or dwarf planet, with 455 confirmed examples across the Solar System's six major systems — what is it called?
Natural satellite: Astronomical body that orbits a planet. Natural satellites are colloquially referred to as moons, by analogy with the Moon, Earth's natural satellite.
This American physicist won the 1989 Nobel for inventing the separated oscillatory field method behind atomic clocks, and helped found both Brookhaven National Laboratory and Fermilab — who was he?

Numbering 126 species, these are the largest order of marsupials in the Western Hemisphere — and only one of them, the Virginia variety, made it as far north as the United States and Canada. What animal is this?

Named after the bones that house them — frontal, maxillary, ethmoid, and sphenoid — these four paired air-filled spaces surround the nasal cavity and have a still-debated evolutionary purpose — what are they called?
Paranasal sinuses: Air-filled spaces surrounding the nasal cavity.
This order of hoofed mammals — horses, rhinos, and tapirs — bears its weight on an odd number of toes and digests plant fiber in its intestines rather than a multi-chambered stomach. Which order?
Perissodactyla: Order of hoofed mammals. Perissodactyla (from Ancient Greek περισσός, perissós 'odd' and δάκτυλος, dáktylos 'finger, toe'), or odd-toed ungulates, is an order of ungulates.
Scientifically named Cajanus cajan, this perennial Fabaceae legume is a staple crop across the Indian subcontinent, Southeast Asia, Africa, and the Caribbean — what is it?
Pigeon pea: Species of perennial legume. The pigeon pea (Cajanus cajan) is a perennial legume from the family Fabaceae native to the Eastern Hemisphere.
Though they look like dolphins, these small toothed whales are actually closer kin to narwhals and belugas, with flat spade-shaped teeth instead of dolphins' cone-shaped ones — what are they called?
Porpoise: Small cetacean of the family Phocoenidae.
This holotropical bird family comprises a dozen Afrotropical species and some 167 Neotropical species, including the blue-and-yellow macaw and the grey parrot — which family is this?
Psittacidae: Family of birds. The family Psittacidae or holotropical parrots is one of three families of true parrots.
After his Jewish family fled Germany, this engineer at Sanders Associates dreamed up playing games on a TV screen and built a 'Brown Box' that became the first home video game console — who is he?
Ralph H. Baer: American inventor and engineer (1922–2014)
This English anatomist coined the word 'Dinosauria' — 'terrible reptile' — yet remained an outspoken critic of Darwin's theory of natural selection — who is it?
Richard Owen: English biologist and palaeontologist (1804–1892)
Also known as brewer's or baker's yeast, this single-celled fungus believed to have originated on grape skins is one of biology's most-studied model organisms — which species?
Saccharomyces cerevisiae: Species of yeast. The species has been instrumental in winemaking, baking, and brewing since ancient times.
This synthetic element, number 106, holds the rare distinction of being named after a scientist who was still alive at the time — its most stable isotopes survive mere minutes. What is it?
Seaborgium: Chemical element with atomic number 106 (Sg)

Usually triggered by a viral infection and common in people with asthma or cystic fibrosis, this inflammation of the facial mucous membranes causes congestion, facial pain, and loss of smell. What condition is it?
Sinusitis: Inflammation of the sinus' membranes. Sinusitis is a condition that affects both children and adults.

Starting from stem cells near the wall of the seminiferous tubules, this multi-stage process runs cells through two rounds of meiosis to turn diploid germ cells into haploid swimmers. What is it called?
Usually caused by Staphylococcus bacteria and treated at home with warm compresses, this tender red bump at the edge of the eyelid is also known as a hordeolum — what is it?
Stye: Swelling of the eyelid due to infection of an oil gland.
This genus contains every living species of a large, snout-nosed herbivorous mammal, including the Malayan form sometimes split into its own genus — what is it?
Tapirus: Genus of tapir. The Malayan tapir is usually included in Tapirus as well, although some authorities have moved it into its own genus, Acrocodia.
As head of Harland and Wolff's drafting department, this shipbuilder helped design the Olympic-class liners and went down with the most famous of them on her maiden voyage — who was he?
Thomas Andrews: British businessman and shipbuilder (1873–1912)
This medication — a synthetic version of the amino building block lysine — helps prevent excessive bleeding from trauma, surgery, or childbirth by blocking clot breakdown — what is it?

German and Russian teams keep trying and failing to synthesize this hypothetical element 120 — an alkaline earth metal of interest because it may sit in the "island of stability." What's its placeholder name?
Unbinilium: Theoretical chemical element with atomic number 120 (Ubn)
Native from Morocco and Portugal east to Iran, this flowering plant species includes thousands of varieties whose fruit is eaten fresh or dried into raisins and currants — what species is it?
Vitis vinifera: Species of flowering plant in the grape vine family.
The largest wild member of the dog family, it can still breed fertile hybrids with coyotes and jackals, and counts the domestic dog and dingo among its many subspecies — what animal is it?
The symbol for roentgenium is Rg. Roentgenium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Rg and atomic number 111.
The symbol for gold is Au. Gold is a chemical element; its chemical symbol is Au and atomic number 79.

Quentin Tarantino: Quentin Jerome Tarantino ( TARR-ən-TEE-noh; born March 27, 1963) is an American filmmaker, actor, and author.

Sean Connery: Sir Thomas Sean Connery (25 August 1930 – 31 October 2020) was a Scottish actor.
In what year was Michael Fassbender born?
Michael Fassbender (German pronunciation: [ˈmɪçaʔeːl ˈfasbɛndɐ]; born 2 April 1977) is a German-Irish actor, racing driver and producer.
In what year was Bob Odenkirk born?
Bob Odenkirk: Robert John Odenkirk (born October 22, 1962) is an American actor, screenwriter, comedian, and producer.
In what year did Catherine O'Hara die?
Catherine O'Hara: Catherine Anne O'Hara (March 4, 1954 – January 30, 2026) was a Canadian and American actress and comedian, whose career spanned over 50 years.
In what year was Licorice Pizza first released?
Licorice Pizza is a 2021 American coming-of-age comedy drama film written and directed by Paul Thomas Anderson.
In what year was The Exorcist: Believer first released?
The Exorcist: Believer: 2023. The sixth installment in The Exorcist franchise, it serves as a legacy sequel to The Exorcist (1973).
In what year was Jeanne du Barry first released?
Jeanne du Barry (film): It also stars Pierre Richard, Benjamin Lavernhe, Noémie Lvovsky, Pascal Greggory, Melvil Poupaud, and India Hair.
